task: Turn these notes into a decision brief in Markdown for the operations VP's Thursday meeting. Use the supplied notes as your source.
source: The VP needs to authorize a six-week help-desk pilot on Thursday. The $18,000 pilot budget includes setup. US data residency and company SSO on day one are mandatory. Atlas costs $14,000 all-in, can start in 10 business days, supports company SSO on day one, and hosts data in the US. It retains audit logs for 30 days. Nova costs $9,000 all-in, can start in five business days, and hosts data in the US. It retains logs for 90 days. Nova can enable company SSO in week five. Security has mentioned an exception process but has granted no exception. Atlas's data processing agreement (DPA) has not cleared Legal. Maya owns the Legal check and expects a decision Tuesday. The team also discussed custom colors, two vendor webinars, and whether to rename the shared test channel. None was identified as a pilot approval criterion.

checks.decision: States that the VP needs to authorize or choose a vendor for the six-week pilot at Thursday's meeting.
checks.recommendation: Recommends Atlas subject to the Legal/DPA check, or clearly makes approval conditional on Legal clearing the DPA.
checks.tradeoff: Accurately contrasts $14,000 versus $9,000 and 10 versus five business days, and explains that Nova misses the mandatory day-one SSO requirement.
checks.open_dependency: Keeps Atlas's DPA clearance open and identifies Maya and Tuesday as the owner and expected timing.
checks.source_fidelity: States no material fact that contradicts the source, and does not present a possible exception or Legal clearance as granted.

task: Write a Markdown impact analysis of this wait-state change for Support, Operations, and Product. They need it for their launch discussion. Use the supplied notes as your source.
source: Today all open return requests stay open indefinitely unless someone closes them. After launch, a return in Awaiting customer documents expires after seven calendar days in that status. The clock starts when the request enters that status, not when it is created. The customer can submit a new request; the expired request stays closed. Requests in Internal review are unaffected. Completed and cancelled records remain untouched. A customer with an expired request will see Expired in their portal. Support needs to explain how to submit a new request. Product has yet to decide whether to apply the rule to requests already open on launch day, and Communications has yet to decide whether to send an expiry email. Example R-82 was created nine days ago and entered Awaiting customer documents two days ago. Under the rule it has five days left in that status, assuming it is in scope. Engineering estimated two points and discussed a button icon, with no committed icon change.

checks.before_after_and_clock: Explains that open requests formerly stayed open until closed and that expiry is seven calendar days counted from entering Awaiting customer documents.
checks.affected_customer: Explains that expiry is visible in the portal, the existing request stays closed, and the customer can submit a new request, with Support responsible for explaining that path.
checks.unaffected_cases: Makes clear that Internal review and already completed or cancelled requests are unaffected.
checks.open_decisions: Keeps both launch-day backfill and the expiry email open, and associates them with Product and Communications respectively.
checks.source_fidelity: States no material fact that contradicts the source. If it includes R-82, it shows five days left conditional on scope, and makes no commitment on backfill or email.

task: Write a Markdown SOP for a new catalog operator to publish a supplier's price list. Use the notes below as the only source.
source: Prerequisites are an approved pricing CSV, the supplier ID, and Catalog Admin access. In Catalog Admin, open Imports, select the supplier ID, upload the CSV, and review the Preview before pressing Publish. Compare the preview's new and updated item counts to the approved file. If duplicate SKUs are flagged, stop; the active catalog is unchanged. Request a corrected file from the supplier and begin again at upload. If any price changes by more than 10%, obtain written approval from Merchandising before publishing. On success, the batch shows Applied. Open two affected SKUs and verify their prices against the approved CSV. Record the batch ID in the change log only after those checks. On a price mismatch, contact Catalog Support without republishing. The old slide deck includes an optional team photo and an overview of the catalog redesign, neither part of the procedure.

checks.prerequisites_and_flow: Names the approved CSV, supplier ID, and Catalog Admin access; sequences selecting supplier, uploading, reviewing preview counts, and then publishing.
checks.duplicate_exception: For duplicate SKUs, says to stop, obtain a corrected file from the supplier, and restart at upload without publishing the flagged batch.
checks.price_exception: Requires written Merchandising approval before publication when any price changes by more than 10%.
checks.completion_and_mismatch: Requires Applied status, matching prices for two affected SKUs, and recording the batch ID afterward; directs mismatches to Catalog Support without republishing.
checks.source_fidelity: States no material fact that contradicts the approved sequence, exception thresholds, approval roles, or recovery rules.
